systems.name: Experience Policy and Session Control
systems.responsibility: Own user-selected replacement goals, active scope, enable/disable controls and explicit failure policy.
systems.boundary: Owns configuration and lifecycle; excludes pixel acquisition, recognition and rendering. Failure behavior remains a user decision.
systems.independence: Can be implemented and tested against mocked pipeline status and versioned configuration contracts.

systems.name: Visual Source Access
systems.responsibility: Obtain permitted source imagery with timing, geometry, color and display identity metadata without altering source application behavior.
systems.boundary: Owns platform-specific acquisition and source eligibility; excludes semantic interpretation and final presentation. Must prevent recapture of its own output where applicable.
systems.independence: Platform adapters can be replaced independently; prerecorded or synthetic frame providers can test downstream systems.

systems.name: Target Recognition and Tracking
systems.responsibility: Locate selected visual targets and maintain consistent identities and masks over time.
systems.boundary: Owns detection, segmentation, temporal tracking and uncertainty reporting; excludes replacement appearance and OS display integration.
systems.independence: Can be evaluated on labeled frame sequences independently of capture and presentation; no model or training strategy selected.

systems.name: Replacement Synthesis and Composition
systems.responsibility: Generate replacement appearance, such as glitter, and composite it into selected regions while preserving unrelated imagery.
systems.boundary: Owns effect generation, occlusion treatment and image composition; excludes target selection policy and final display control.
systems.independence: Can consume recorded frames and masks to validate visual quality; effects can change without replacing recognition or platform adapters.

systems.name: Presentation and Display Integration
systems.responsibility: Deliver modified imagery to the user with correct alignment and timing while leaving normal input directed to underlying applications.
systems.boundary: Owns platform-specific presentation, output scheduling and applicable focus/input-transparency behavior; excludes game logic, input synthesis and target recognition. Capture-plus-overlay versus an authorized pre-display integration is deliberately unresolved.
systems.independence: Can be tested using synthetic modified frames and input/focus checks. Realization depends on platform capabilities; conceptual separation does not imply unrestricted OS access.

interfaces.exchange: Versioned capture scope, session state and permission intent; eligibility, permission failures and frame-source status returned.
Versioned target definitions and selected scopes; confidence and unsupported-target status returned.
Replacement style parameters and policy version; effect availability and processing status returned.
Enable/disable, selected output, user-approved fallback policy and timing constraints; presentation health and capability status returned.
Immutable frame reference with frame ID, timestamp, dimensions, coordinate mapping and color metadata.
Same source frame reference and metadata, synchronized by frame ID; bounded buffer ownership and release contract.
Frame-keyed target masks, track IDs and confidence/uncertainty; missing or stale masks explicitly marked.
Completed frame or replacement-layer reference, frame ID, source geometry, timestamps and completeness status; buffer release and backpressure returned.
Output surface identity and display geometry changes for feedback-loop avoidance and coordinate agreement.

research_basis: User-provided requirement: replace blood in a game with glitter as an example, eventually across the desktop, without changing game behavior or normal interaction.

Official Microsoft documentation states Desktop Duplication provides access to desktop images and protects protected video content: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/display/desktop-duplication-api . This supports investigating an acquisition adapter, not a claim that captured images can replace the physical display.

Official Apple documentation describes ScreenCaptureKit desktop/app/window capture and screen-recording permission: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/ScreenCaptureKit?language=objc . This supports a permission-aware platform adapter, not a validated presentation approach.

Engineering proposal, not experimentally verified: separate acquisition, semantic recognition, effect composition and presentation so that platform integration and replacement algorithms can evolve independently.
Unvalidated hypothesis: image-based recognition and temporally stable replacement can meet the user's quality and latency requirements. No benchmark, model evaluation or prototype has been performed.

Critical unresolved feasibility distinction: acquiring screen imagery is not the same as controlling what reaches the display. A capture-and-overlay design must not be represented as guaranteeing that original content is never seen. Platform-specific validation is required before choosing an implementation.
Proposed conservative baseline, not a user-stated requirement: process transient frames on-device without persistence; confirm privacy and retention requirements before implementation.
open_questions: Which initial OS, hardware, game and display mode define the first feasibility test?
Can original content briefly appear, or must every displayed frame be filtered before visibility? This may change the display integration architecture.
What latency, frame rate, resolution, detection-error and temporal-stability targets define success?
What is the required behavior when a target is uncertain, a deadline is missed, access is denied, or the pipeline fails?
Can an authorized presentation path cover required fullscreen/desktop scenarios while preserving input and focus and avoiding capture feedback? This is not established by the capture documentation.
How will recognition generalize beyond the initial game, and what labeled data or user configuration is available?
What desktop-wide coverage limitations, protected-content exclusions and anti-cheat compatibility constraints are acceptable?
Must source pixels remain local and transient, and should screenshots or streams contain the original or modified view?
